retired.reason: Discharged by W48-QR-FLOAT-IEEE-LEAN-MODEL for the arithmetic half: QCore.Ieee754 (encoding, round trips, class partition), QCore.Ieee754Round (round to nearest, ties to even, subnormals, overflow; nearest, tie, monotone, exact, overflow threshold), QCore.Ieee754Ops (+ - * /, negation, comparisons, int -> float, f64 -> f32, f32 -> f64, float -> int; special-case table; gated operators mean the IEEE relations; int -> float equal to QCore.FloatTypes.roundNat), and the Rust kernel's vector tables (4,006 rows, 19,171 results) proved against the model by kernel computation and regenerated by compiler/tests/float_ieee_vectors.rs. The renderer's digit search is not proved and moves to W48-QR-FLOAT-RENDER-ROUNDTRIP-PROOF.

registered.title: The `dec` renderer's shortest round-trip property is observed, not proved
registered.why: Found by W48-QR-FLOAT-IEEE-LEAN-MODEL (item 5 of its brief, the stretch, not reached). The IEEE model (`QCore.Ieee754*`) states the values `f32`/`f64` patterns denote and the rounding of an exact rational to them, but not the Dragon4 shortest-digit search that `scalar_floats::shortest_digits` (Rust's formatting) and the emitted C renderer perform: neither that the `dec` digits read back to the same value (decimal parsing = `round` of the decimal's exact rational, which the model now has) nor that no shorter decimal does is proved, and the emitted renderer's agreement with Rust stays observed on the boundary table and seeded sample (specification §L14.7, limitation 13). Size M. DISCHARGE: a Lean digit search (or a checked characterisation of the shortest digits) proved to read back through `QCore.Ieee754.round` and to be shortest, bound to Rust vectors over the boundary table and powers of two.

registered.title: `QCore.FloatTypes.toInt` admits `bool` as a float → integer target; the kernel does not
registered.why: Found by W48-QR-FLOAT-IEEE-LEAN-MODEL. The float card's `QCore.FloatTypes.toInt t .bool x` truncates and succeeds when the truncation is 0 or 1 (`fits` gives `bool` the range 0..1), while `scalar_types::convert(F32|F64, Bool, …)` is `None` (a float `as bool` is no conversion). Every float → integer vector either model replays uses an integer target, so no replayed row disagrees; the new model's `QCore.Ieee754.toInt` refuses `.bool` (`toInt_bool`), and `QCore.FloatTypes` was not edited (the card's rule). Size S. DISCHARGE: `QCore.FloatTypes.toInt` refusing `.bool` (its theorems restated for integer targets), or a stated reason the difference is harmless, with a `.bool` row in its vector table.
